title: The general and the charioteer of the passions
english: A general captures a city once and then orders it as he pleases. But the charioteer of the passions must keep bringing them into subjection for as long as he lives. The internal enemy is altogether harder to face than the enemy outside. The man who has sacked a city is free from care afterward, but the one who faces an unceasing enemy must keep struggling. To master anger, then, is a great achievement, and a great victory over the spirit of anger.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is contrasting a military general who captures a city once with the person who must continually rule the passions throughout life.

title: Evil desire as prostitute drowning the mind
english: Not only has it been said concerning a prostitute, but also concerning evil desire. For when the mind sets itself toward wicked action, then the heart meditates the crooked things which the mouth speaks. For then the mind will be as in the heart of the sea, by the brine of its many thoughts.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius continues his commentary by explaining that the prostitute in Proverbs signifies evil desire, which overwhelms the mind like a pilot in a storm and drives it toward wicked action.

title: The mind drowned by evil desire
english: The mind is overwhelmed like a pilot in a heavy swell. Driven by the waves of evil desire, it struggles in anguish as it is forced toward the wicked act.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is closing his comment on the prostitute passage, explaining that it also describes evil desire overwhelming the mind.
